Fewer public entry points and unified ggplot2 graphics in 0.3.0

Source: R/help_api_migration_030.R, R/help_compatibility_layer.R, R/help_plot_migration.R
mfrmr_api_migration_030.Rd

Related operations now use arguments or standard S3 methods, and all plot() methods render and return ggplot2 objects directly. Because overlapping entry points are no longer exported and plot() returns a ggplot object rather than mfrm_plot_data / base graphics, version 0.3.0 uses a minor-version increment under semantic versioning: review existing 0.2.x scripts when updating to 0.3.0. Existing saved result classes retain their summary(), plot(), plot_data(), and as_ggplot() methods.

Usage

compatibility_alias_table(
  scope = c("all", "functions", "arguments", "fields", "columns", "plot_metrics")
)

Arguments

scope

Which alias surface to return in compatibility_alias_table(): "all", "functions", "arguments", "fields", "columns", or "plot_metrics".

Value

compatibility_alias_table() returns a data.frame with columns Alias, PreferredName, Surface, Lifecycle ("retained_alias" or "removed_export"), RetainedFor, RemovalPlan, and Notes.

Default route guide

mfrmr_output_guide() now returns the five central routes, matching scope = "core_workflow". Use mfrmr_output_guide("all") where a script needs the former full catalogue. Explicit scopes, including the six-row "public" and "beginner" routes, retain their meanings and columns.

Argument and saved-result migration notes:

  • Reports (mfrm_report()): Rename fit/dif_result to x and pass full type names ("iterations" vs "bias_iterations").

  • Clustering (mfrm_cluster()): Pass method-specific controls (linkage, seed, etc.) by name; unsupported controls fail closed.

  • Calibration (update()): Rename calibration to object and state-specific timestamps to at_utc (validated -> frozen; superseded / retired require a distinct record_id).

  • ConQuest files (normalize_conquest_overlap_tables(..., input = "files")): Rename population_file, item_file, and case_file to conquest_population, conquest_item_estimates, and conquest_case_eap.

Score-comparison columns

The former automated-scoring interface now uses score_comparison_table(). Keep categories, supply continuous scores' explicit score_categories, and choose screen = "williamson2012" to retain the earlier thresholds. Without that choice the generic default applies no thresholds. Rename smd = "human" to smd = "reference", including SMDBasis and settings$smd; the corresponding criteria$Basis suffix is now _smd_reference. These are naming changes, not different denominators.

Former table columnCurrent table column
HumanReferenceSuppliedReference2Supplied
MeanAutomated, MeanHumanMeanScore, MeanReference
SDAutomated, SDHumanSDScore, SDReference
HumanQWK, HumanCorrelationReferenceQWK, ReferenceCorrelation
SMDHumanSMDReference

In cases, rename MissingAutomated to MissingScore, MissingHuman to MissingReference, MissingAutomatedCategory to MissingScoreCategory, and MissingHumanReference to MissingReference2. In counts, rename automated_human/human_human to scores_reference/reference2_reference; the second dimension is now named Reference rather than Human. Saved earlier lists keep their original names and can be reopened with readRDS() without a model refit.

Unified ggplot2 return contract

All plot() S3 methods now render with ggplot2 (ggplot2 (>= 3.4.0) in Imports) and invisibly return a ggplot object (inherits(p, "ggplot")). Setting draw = FALSE constructs and returns the ggplot object without printing it or opening a graphics device.

Update scripts that previously indexed p$data$... on a returned mfrm_plot_data list to call plot_data() (plot_data(p) for the full payload list, plot_data(p, component = ...) for a named table/matrix, or plot_data(p, "notes") for descriptions and cautions) and plot_data_components() to inspect available components.

Saved plot payloads from 0.2.x (mfrm_plot_data, mfrm_design_evaluation_plot_data, and mfrm_signal_detection_plot_data) remain compatible with both plot_data() and as_ggplot(), and calling as_ggplot(p) on a 0.3.0 ggplot return value is idempotent. Two-continuous-variable scatterplots (including the new plot(dif, type = "scatter") route after analyze_dff(), model comparisons, fit pathway, fair average, bias, PCA scores, and recovery scatterplots) add aligned X/Y marginal histograms via marginal = c("auto", "histogram", "none"). These changes do not add support for previously unsupported models or uncertainty calculations.

Structured fit_mfrm() signature and shared spec

fit_mfrm() now exposes a focused 19-argument signature (data, 15 common model/design arguments, spec = NULL, control = list(), and ...) that partitions all 55 canonical arguments into data (1), spec (33 model, scale, identification, anchor, interaction, and population keys), and control (21 quadrature, optimizer, shrinkage, JML correction, and runtime keys).

  • Full-name flat arguments remain supported: Supply the complete names of the 55 canonical arguments directly to fit_mfrm() or in the named list passed to do.call(fit_mfrm, ...). Their defaults and statistical meaning are unchanged. Only the first four positional arguments (data, person, facets, score) retain their old positions; name all later arguments. Abbreviations for arguments now routed through ... are rejected. For example, replace quad_point = 15 with quad_points = 15 or control = list(quad_points = 15).

  • Shared 4-entrypoint spec: One named spec = list(...) can be passed unchanged to describe_mfrm_data(), review_mfrm_anchors(), fit_mfrm(), and export_mfrm_model() (data = ..., spec = spec) within each function's supported scope. A valid native fit specification is not necessarily exportable: ordinary RSM/PCM export requires a fixed standard-normal population; estimated intercept-only normal populations are supported only for one-family GPCM in Stan. Explicit top-level arguments override entries in spec; misplaced or duplicated keys fail with actionable guidance.

  • Technical reference page: Specialist equations, identification rules, JML polish-ladder details, and return-object provenance now live in fit_mfrm_technical_details (linked from fit_mfrm()). Use mfrmr_output_guide("core_workflow") for the purpose-based analysis map.

For an existing rating table ratings with scores 1–4, these calls show how to migrate partial names and positional arguments. Run only the current form:

# Old: fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
#               1, 4, method = "MML", model = "RSM", quad_point = 15)
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  ratings, person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
  method = "MML", model = "RSM",
  control = list(quad_points = 15)
)

The example preserves the old default model constraints. Migration does not establish that those constraints are suitable for a particular assessment; review the population and location assumptions in fit_mfrm().

Saved-analysis refresh and compatibility surface

Installing an update does not recalculate saved objects on disk. Check summary(fit)$decision first: if an early saved fit lacks current terminal-gradient or category-support checks, refit from the original data and settings; otherwise regenerate affected diagnose_mfrm(), compare_mfrm(), analyze_dff(), estimate_bias(), compute_facet_icc(), or predict_mfrm_units() outputs from the saved fit before rebuilding reports or CSV exports. Saved 0.2.x G-Study/D-Study and plot payloads (mfrm_plot_data) work directly with summary(), plot(), plot_data(), and as_ggplot().

Legacy FACETS-oriented wrappers (run_mfrm_facets(), build_fixed_reports(), facets_output_file_bundle(), write_mfrm_residual_file(), write_mfrm_subset_file()) are presentation and handoff contracts, not claims of FACETS, ConQuest, or SPSS numerical equivalence.

Former 0.2.4 plot helper replacements

In 0.3.0, every plot() S3 method renders with ggplot2 and invisibly returns a ggplot object (draw = FALSE suppresses device output; extract underlying tables and notes with plot_data() and plot_data_components()). Replace the 33 former plot_*() helpers with plot() on the corresponding fitted model or analysis result:

Former exported helperReplacement
plot_anchor_drift()plot(x)
plot_apa_figure_one()plot(x, type = "apa_summary")
plot_bias_interaction()plot(x, type = "bias")
plot_bubble()plot(x, type = "bubble")
plot_compare_mfrm()plot(reference, comparison = comparison)
plot_dif_heatmap() / plot_dif_summary()plot(x, type = "heatmap") / plot(x, type = "summary")
plot_displacement()plot(x, type = "displacement")
plot_facet_equivalence()plot(x, type = "facet_equivalence")
plot_facet_quality_dashboard()plot(x, type = "facet_dashboard")
plot_facets_chisq()plot(x, type = "facets_chisq")
plot_fair_average()plot(x, type = "fair_average")
plot_guttman_scalogram()plot(x, type = "guttman")
plot_information()plot(x)
plot_interrater_agreement()plot(x, type = "agreement")
plot_local_dependence_heatmap()plot(x, type = "local_dependence")
plot_marginal_fit() / plot_marginal_pairwise()plot(x, type = "marginal_fit") / type = "marginal_pairwise"
plot_person_fit()plot(x, type = "person_fit")
plot_qc_dashboard() / plot_qc_pipeline()plot(x, type = "qc") / plot(x)
plot_rater_agreement_heatmap()plot(x, type = "agreement", view = "heatmap")
plot_rater_severity_profile()plot(x, type = "rater_severity")
plot_rater_trajectory()plot(fits[[1L]], type = "trajectory", comparison = fits[-1L], labels = names(fits))
plot_reliability_snapshot()plot(x, type = "reliability")
plot_residual_matrix() / plot_residual_pca() / plot_residual_qq()plot(x, type = "residual_matrix") / "residual_pca" / "residual_qq"
plot_response_time_review()plot(x)
plot_shrinkage_funnel()plot(x, type = "shrinkage", view = "funnel")
plot_threshold_ladder()plot(x, type = "thresholds")
plot_unexpected()plot(x, type = "unexpected")
